newsitem.title: UK: CBI welcomes budget PSBR cuts, wary of tax changes.
newsitem.headline: CBI welcomes budget PSBR cuts, wary of tax changes.

text.p: The Confederation of British Industry said it welcomed the reduction in government borrowing outlined in Tuesday's UK budget speech but it was concerned about the number of tax changes adding to business costs.
The phased abolition of profit-related pay, meantime, is likely to be a setback for the spread of employee financial participation, the CBI said in a brief post-budget statement.
"We welcome the overall reduction in public borrowing, which will keep it on a firmly downward path," the CBI statement said.
However, the CBI said it needed to look closely at the details of public spending cuts and the balance between real sustainable reductions and one-off measures in particular.

"There are concerns about the number of tax changes which will add to business costs," the CBI added. "In particular, the less favourable treatment of capital allowances for long-life assets is unwelcome as are the hikes in airport duties and insurance premium tax."
